_comment: Family-friendly 'ask, don't tell' prompt per misconception tag, used by the Play-tab card 'Play the Confused Grown-Up' (scripts/lib/homework-confused-grownup.mjs). Each entry is derived from that tag's `watchFor` in engine/core/misconceptions.js (data/misconception-taxonomy.json); `watchFor` is copied here so tools/homework-confused-grownup.test.mjs fails when the taxonomy changes and the prompt was not revisited. A tag with no entry here is never used by the card.

algebra-distributive-partial.watchFor: Draw the area model — the outside factor touches BOTH terms.
algebra-distributive-partial.askEn: Draw a box to show it. Which pieces does the outside number touch?
algebra-distributive-partial.askEs: Dibuja un rectángulo para mostrarlo. ¿Con cuáles partes se relaciona el número de afuera?

coord-xy-swapped.watchFor: Have them trace the horizontal move with a finger before the vertical one.
coord-xy-swapped.askEn: Trace the sideways move with your finger first. Which number told you how far across to go?
coord-xy-swapped.askEs: Traza primero con el dedo el movimiento de lado. ¿Cuál número te dijo cuánto avanzar de lado?

decimal-place-value.watchFor: Estimate to the nearest whole first, then count decimal places out loud.
decimal-place-value.askEn: Round to the nearest whole number first. About how big should the answer be? Then count the decimal places out loud.
decimal-place-value.askEs: Redondea primero al número entero más cercano. ¿Más o menos qué tan grande debe ser la respuesta? Luego cuenta los lugares decimales en voz alta.

division-quotient-missing-zero.watchFor: Estimate first — 4,896 ÷ 12 is about 400, not 40 — then check the quotient has a digit above every digit that was brought down.
division-quotient-missing-zero.askEn: Estimate first: about how big should the answer be? Does your answer have a digit above every digit that came down?
division-quotient-missing-zero.askEs: Estima primero: ¿más o menos qué tan grande debe ser la respuesta? ¿Tu respuesta tiene un dígito encima de cada dígito que bajó?

equation-answered-with-given-number.watchFor: Ask them to substitute their answer back into the original equation out loud.
equation-answered-with-given-number.askEn: Put your answer back into the original equation and say it out loud. Does it make a true statement?
equation-answered-with-given-number.askEs: Pon tu respuesta de vuelta en la ecuación original y léela en voz alta. ¿Es una afirmación verdadera?

equation-not-inverse-operation.watchFor: Have them name the operation acting on the variable BEFORE they touch both sides.
equation-not-inverse-operation.askEn: What is being done to the letter? Say it, then say what undoes it.
equation-not-inverse-operation.askEs: ¿Qué se le está haciendo a la letra? Dilo, y luego di qué lo deshace.

exponent-as-multiplication.watchFor: Expand it once — write out every factor before evaluating.
exponent-as-multiplication.askEn: Write the exponent out as repeated factors, one factor at a time. What do you get?
exponent-as-multiplication.askEs: Escribe el exponente como factores repetidos, un factor a la vez. ¿Qué obtienes?

factorization-stopped-early.watchFor: Point at each factor and ask: can this one still be broken apart?
factorization-stopped-early.askEn: Point to each factor. Can this one still be broken into smaller factors?
factorization-stopped-early.askEs: Señala cada factor. ¿Este todavía se puede separar en factores más pequeños?

factors-multiples-confused.watchFor: Ask which number divides which — factors go INTO it, multiples come OUT of it.
factors-multiples-confused.askEn: Which number divides evenly into which?
factors-multiples-confused.askEs: ¿Cuál número se divide exactamente entre cuál?

fraction-no-reciprocal.watchFor: Ask them to check with a whole-number case they already trust.
fraction-no-reciprocal.askEn: Try the same idea on a whole-number problem you already trust. Does your method still work?
fraction-no-reciprocal.askEs: Prueba la misma idea con un problema de números enteros que ya conoces bien. ¿Tu método sigue funcionando?

fraction-straight-across-division.watchFor: Reground division as “how many of these fit into that?”
fraction-straight-across-division.askEn: Ask yourself: how many of these fit into that? Does your answer match that story?
fraction-straight-across-division.askEs: Pregúntate: ¿cuántos de estos caben en aquel? ¿Tu respuesta coincide con esa historia?

geom-surface-area-as-volume.watchFor: Ask what the unit has to be — square units cover a surface, cubic units fill a space.
geom-surface-area-as-volume.askEn: What units must the answer have: square units that cover a surface, or cubic units that fill a space?
geom-surface-area-as-volume.askEs: ¿Qué unidades debe tener la respuesta: unidades cuadradas que cubren una superficie o unidades cúbicas que llenan un espacio?

geom-triangle-area-no-half.watchFor: Draw the rectangle around the triangle — the triangle is half of it.
geom-triangle-area-no-half.askEn: Draw a rectangle around the triangle. How does the triangle compare with the rectangle?
geom-triangle-area-no-half.askEs: Dibuja un rectángulo alrededor del triángulo. ¿Cómo se compara el triángulo con el rectángulo?

geom-volume-added-dimensions.watchFor: Build one layer of unit cubes first, then count the layers.
geom-volume-added-dimensions.askEn: Picture one layer of unit cubes first. How many layers are there?
geom-volume-added-dimensions.askEs: Imagina primero una capa de cubos unitarios. ¿Cuántas capas hay?

inequality-boundary-inclusion.watchFor: Have them test the boundary value itself — does it make the statement true?
inequality-boundary-inclusion.askEn: Try the boundary number itself. Does it make the statement true?
inequality-boundary-inclusion.askEs: Prueba el número del límite. ¿Hace verdadera la afirmación?

inequality-direction-flipped.watchFor: Ask which moves can flip a symbol — adding and subtracting never do.
inequality-direction-flipped.askEn: Which kinds of moves can flip the symbol? Did we make one of those moves here?
inequality-direction-flipped.askEs: ¿Qué tipos de pasos pueden voltear el símbolo? ¿Hicimos alguno de esos pasos aquí?

inequality-graph-direction.watchFor: Make them test one number from the shaded side out loud before accepting a graph.
inequality-graph-direction.askEn: Pick one number from the shaded side. Does it make the statement true?
inequality-graph-direction.askEs: Elige un número del lado sombreado. ¿Hace verdadera la afirmación?

measure-area-perimeter-swap.watchFor: Ask what the unit should be — units or square units?
measure-area-perimeter-swap.askEn: What units should the answer have: units, or square units? How do you know?
measure-area-perimeter-swap.askEs: ¿Qué unidades debe tener la respuesta: unidades o unidades cuadradas? ¿Cómo lo sabes?

op-added-instead-of-multiplied.watchFor: Ask what the operation *does* to the quantity before they compute.
op-added-instead-of-multiplied.askEn: What is happening to the amount in this story: are we joining amounts, or making equal groups?
op-added-instead-of-multiplied.askEs: ¿Qué le pasa a la cantidad en esta historia: juntamos cantidades o hacemos grupos iguales?

op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.watchFor: Estimate first — should the answer be bigger or smaller than you started?
op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.askEn: Before we compute, should the answer end up bigger or smaller than the number we started with?
op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.askEs: Antes de calcular, ¿la respuesta debe quedar mayor o menor que el número con el que empezamos?

op-multiplied-instead-of-added.watchFor: Have them restate the problem as a story, then name the operation.
op-multiplied-instead-of-added.askEn: Tell me the problem as a little story. What is happening to the amounts in it?
op-multiplied-instead-of-added.askEs: Cuéntame el problema como una historia corta. ¿Qué les pasa a las cantidades?

op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.watchFor: Estimate first — should the answer be bigger or smaller than you started?
op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.askEn: Before we compute, should the answer be bigger or smaller than the number we started with?
op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.askEs: Antes de calcular, ¿la respuesta debe ser mayor o menor que el número con el que empezamos?

op-reversed-division.watchFor: Ask “what is being split, and into how many?” before they write it.
op-reversed-division.askEn: What is being split up, and how many parts is it split into?
op-reversed-division.askEs: ¿Qué se está repartiendo y en cuántas partes se reparte?

op-reversed-subtraction.watchFor: Anchor both numbers on a number line before subtracting.
op-reversed-subtraction.askEn: Mark both numbers on a number line. Where do we start, and which way do we move?
op-reversed-subtraction.askEs: Marca los dos números en una recta numérica. ¿Dónde empezamos y hacia qué lado nos movemos?

order-of-operations-left-to-right.watchFor: Have them circle the operation that must go first, then compute.
order-of-operations-left-to-right.askEn: Circle the operation that has to go first. Why does it go first?
order-of-operations-left-to-right.askEs: Encierra en un círculo la operación que va primero. ¿Por qué va primero?

pattern-unit-position-miscounted.watchFor: Ask them to divide by the unit length out loud and say what the remainder points at.
pattern-unit-position-miscounted.askEn: Divide by the length of one repeating unit, out loud. What does the remainder point to?
pattern-unit-position-miscounted.askEs: Divide entre la longitud de una unidad que se repite, en voz alta. ¿A qué señala el residuo?

percent-scale-off-by-100.watchFor: Benchmark against 50% and 10% before trusting the number.
percent-scale-off-by-100.askEn: Compare with 50% and 10% first. Is your answer about the right size?
percent-scale-off-by-100.askEs: Compara primero con el 50 % y el 10 %. ¿Tu respuesta tiene más o menos el tamaño correcto?

percent-used-as-whole-number.watchFor: Make them say the percent as “per hundred” out loud.
percent-used-as-whole-number.askEn: Say the percent as “per hundred” out loud. What does “per hundred” tell you to do?
percent-used-as-whole-number.askEs: Di el porcentaje como “por cada cien” en voz alta. ¿Qué te indica “por cada cien”?

property-order-vs-grouping.watchFor: Ask what actually MOVED: the order of the numbers, or the parentheses?
property-order-vs-grouping.askEn: What moved: the order of the numbers, or the parentheses?
property-order-vs-grouping.askEs: ¿Qué se movió: el orden de los números o los paréntesis?

rate-not-per-one.watchFor: Ask “per ONE what?” and make them finish the sentence.
rate-not-per-one.askEn: Ask “per ONE what?” and finish the sentence out loud.
rate-not-per-one.askEs: Pregunta «¿por UN qué?» y termina la oración en voz alta.

ratio-as-difference.watchFor: Have them say the comparison out loud — “for every ___ there are ___” — before writing anything.
ratio-as-difference.askEn: Say it with “for every ___ there are ___.” What two amounts are you comparing?
ratio-as-difference.askEs: Dilo con “por cada ___ hay ___”. ¿Qué dos cantidades estás comparando?

ratio-compared-without-common-basis.watchFor: Ask what ONE of each is worth before either ratio is compared.
ratio-compared-without-common-basis.askEn: What is ONE of each worth, before we compare the two?
ratio-compared-without-common-basis.askEs: ¿Cuánto vale UNO de cada uno, antes de comparar los dos?

ratio-inverted.watchFor: Have them label both quantities with units before writing the ratio.
ratio-inverted.askEn: Say what each number counts, with its unit. Which one does the question name first?
ratio-inverted.askEs: Di qué cuenta cada número, con su unidad. ¿Cuál nombra primero la pregunta?

ratio-scaled-additively.watchFor: Ask what ONE batch is worth, then how many batches — a ratio grows by copies, not by steps.
ratio-scaled-additively.askEn: How much is ONE batch? How many batches do we have?

sign-dropped.watchFor: Place the answer on a number line — which side of zero?
sign-dropped.askEn: Put the answer on a number line. Which side of zero is it on?
sign-dropped.askEs: Ubica la respuesta en una recta numérica. ¿De qué lado del cero queda?

stat-center-vs-spread.watchFor: Ask what the question wants to know: a typical value, or how scattered the data is?
stat-center-vs-spread.askEn: What does the question want to know: a typical value, or how spread out the data is?
stat-center-vs-spread.askEs: ¿Qué quiere saber la pregunta: un valor típico o qué tan dispersos están los datos?

stat-frequency-vs-value.watchFor: Ask them to point at the axis their number came from before they answer.
stat-frequency-vs-value.askEn: Point to the axis your number came from. What does that axis count?
stat-frequency-vs-value.askEs: Señala el eje de donde salió tu número. ¿Qué cuenta ese eje?

stat-histogram-bin-misread.watchFor: Have them point to the interval's two endpoints and say which values belong inside it.
stat-histogram-bin-misread.askEn: Point to the two ends of the interval. Which values belong inside it?
stat-histogram-bin-misread.askEs: Señala los dos extremos del intervalo. ¿Cuáles valores pertenecen dentro de él?

stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.watchFor: Have them cover the outlier and recompute — how far does the mean move?
stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.askEn: Cover the outlier and find the mean again. How far did the mean move?
stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.askEs: Tapa el valor atípico y vuelve a hallar la media. ¿Cuánto se movió la media?

stat-mean-vs-median.watchFor: Ask them to say which word the question used, then what that word tells you to DO with the numbers.
stat-mean-vs-median.askEn: Which word did the question use? What does that word tell you to do with the numbers?
stat-mean-vs-median.askEs: ¿Qué palabra usó la pregunta? ¿Qué te indica esa palabra que hagas con los números?

stat-question-no-variability.watchFor: Ask: would two different people give two different answers?
stat-question-no-variability.askEn: Would two different people give different answers to this question?
stat-question-no-variability.askEs: ¿Dos personas distintas darían respuestas diferentes a esta pregunta?

stat-range-for-iqr.watchFor: Have them mark Q1 and Q3 on the plot and cover everything outside them.
stat-range-for-iqr.askEn: Mark Q1 and Q3 on the plot, then cover everything outside them. What is left?
stat-range-for-iqr.askEs: Marca Q1 y Q3 en la gráfica y tapa todo lo que queda afuera. ¿Qué queda?

stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.watchFor: Ask whether the answer could be a realistic single value in that set.
stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.askEn: Could one typical number from this set really be that big? Does your answer make sense?
stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.askEs: ¿Un número típico de este conjunto podría ser realmente así de grande? ¿Tiene sentido tu respuesta?
